items.title_en: Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes
items.title_zh: Urbex：面向城市级3D场景的智能体空间定位
items.abstract_en: City-scale 3D grounding is commonly formulated as candidate ranking, which requires precomputed instance proposals and becomes inefficient in large outdoor scenes. We propose Urbex, an agentic vision-language framework that instead casts grounding as active spatial search. Urbex represents a city-scale 3D scene as an interactive multi-view environment, allowing a VLM agent to query landmarks, zoom into local regions, render oblique views, and commit a grounded bounding box. We optimize this tool-use policy with reinforcement learning on CityRefer, using smooth localization rewards and lightweight shaping rewards for efficient exploration. Experiments show that Urbex achieves the best Hit@1 and IoU on CityRefer, supports candidate-free grounding without ground-truth boxes, and is substantially faster than the strongest city-scale ranking baseline. Zero-shot results on STPLS3D-Refer further indicate improved cross-scene robustness.
items.abstract_zh: 城市级3D定位通常被建模为候选排序，需要预先计算实例候选框，在大规模户外场景中效率低下。我们提出 Urbex，一个智能体式视觉-语言框架，将定位重新表述为主动空间搜索。Urbex 把城市级3D场景表示为可交互的多视角环境，使 VLM 智能体能够查询地标、放大局部区域、渲染斜视视角，并最终给出定位好的边界框。我们在 CityRefer 上以强化学习优化这一工具使用策略，采用平滑定位奖励与轻量塑形奖励以实现高效探索。实验表明，Urbex 在 CityRefer 上取得最佳 Hit@1 与 IoU，支持无需候选框、无需真值框的定位，且速度显著快于最强的城市级排序基线。在 STPLS3D-Refer 上的零样本结果进一步显示其跨场景鲁棒性有所提升。
items.highlight_zh: 将城市级3D定位重构为智能体主动搜索，免候选框且更快
items.digest_zh:
1）研究问题：给定一句自然语言描述，在城市级3D场景中找出对应物体的位置。传统做法是先离线算出成千上万个候选实例框、再逐一排序，在户外大场景中既慢又依赖大量预处理。
2）方法：Urbex 换了思路，把定位当作“主动找路”。它把整座城市的3D场景变成一个可交互的多视角环境，让视觉语言模型（VLM）像人一样调用工具：先查询地标、放大某片区域、渲染斜视角，最后确认并输出一个边界框。作者用强化学习训练这套“用工具”的策略，奖励上用平滑的定位奖励配合轻量塑形奖励，让探索更高效。
3）结果：在 CityRefer 数据集上，Urbex 的 Hit@1 和 IoU 均为最好；它不需要预先给定候选框，也不需要真值框；速度明显快于最强的城市级排序基线。迁移到 STPLS3D-Refer 做零样本测试时，跨场景表现也更稳健。
4）意义：这说明“让模型主动搜索”比“排序一堆候选”更适合城市级3D理解，摆脱了对候选生成与真值框的依赖，为大规模户外场景中的智能体式空间推理提供了新范式。

rm.usage: 城市级文本指代式3D场景定位与赛场雷达的全场目标检测/坐标解算不是同一问题，关联很弱；仅“查询地标、放大局部、主动搜索”的智能体式搜索思路或可借鉴到雷达多相机调度，但需大改。

items.title_en: GreenWAM: A World Foundation Model for Robotics
items.title_zh: GreenWAM：面向机器人学的世界基础模型
items.abstract_en: A robot needs a world model that predicts how its actions will change the scene and a policy that chooses those actions. Models are usually built and evaluated for only one of these roles, and every robot records its actions in its own format. We ask whether one robot world model can serve both roles across different bodies, and what makes this work. We present GreenWAM, a world foundation model for robotics, together with the recipe that produces it: (1) a shared anatomical action space that describes 20 robot families, from bimanual arms to dexterous humanoids, in common joint coordinates; (2) joint training on these families in visual, action-conditioned and world-action modes; and (3) policies that split an action expert off the generator. As a world model, GreenWAM attains top-tier trajectory, depth and 3D accuracy on WorldArena 1.0, ahead of every world-action model and video generator in our comparison. As a policy, it scores among the top entries of the RoboTwin 2.0 leaderboard, reaches the highest zero-shot LIBERO-plus success among the compared methods and is competitive with dedicated vision-language-action and world-action policies on CALVIN and LIBERO. We further adapt GreenWAM to a real humanoid, where it succeeds more often than policies adapted from $π_{0.5}$ and from Cosmos 3 Edge, and distill it into a single-step policy for real-time control. Controlled experiments yield three findings: robot specialization improves world prediction and control together; an action expert helps when split off at the start of adaptation; and keeping world-model modes during policy adaptation preserves robustness to scene changes.
items.abstract_zh: 机器人既需要一个预测自身动作将如何改变场景的世界模型，也需要一个选择动作的策略。现有模型通常只针对其中一种角色构建与评估，且每个机器人都用自己的格式记录动作。我们追问：一个机器人世界模型能否跨不同本体同时承担这两种角色，以及其成功的关键是什么。我们提出 GreenWAM——一个机器人世界基础模型，并给出其构建配方：（1）共享解剖学动作空间，用统一关节坐标描述从双臂机械臂到灵巧人形共20个机器人家族；（2）在这些家族上以视觉、动作条件和世界-动作三种模式联合训练；（3）从生成器中拆分出动作专家以形成策略。作为世界模型，GreenWAM 在 WorldArena 1.0 上的轨迹、深度与3D精度均达顶尖水平，优于我们对比中的全部世界-动作模型与视频生成器；作为策略，它在 RoboTwin 2.0 排行榜中位居前列，在所比较方法中取得最高的零样本 LIBERO-plus 成功率，并在 CALVIN 与 LIBERO 上与专门的视觉-语言-动作及世界-动作策略相当。我们还将其适配到真实人形机器人，成功率高于由 π0.5 和 Cosmos 3 Edge 适配而来的策略，并将其蒸馏为单步策略以实现实时控制。控制实验得出三点发现：机器人特化能同时改善世界预测与控制；动作专家在适配开始时即拆分更有效；策略适配期间保留世界模型模式有助于维持对场景变化的鲁棒性。
items.highlight_zh: 一个世界模型兼顾预测与策略，跨20种机器人本体通用
items.digest_zh:
1）研究问题：机器人需要两种能力——世界模型（预测动作会让场景怎么变）和策略（决定该做什么动作）。但现有模型往往只做其中一件事，而且每家的机器人动作记录格式都不同，难以通用。作者追问：一个模型能否跨本体同时做好这两件事？
2）方法：GreenWAM 世界基础模型及其“配方”包含三步：一是共享的解剖学动作空间，用统一关节坐标描述20个机器人家族，从双臂机械臂到灵巧人形；二是在视觉、动作条件、世界-动作三种模式下对这些家族联合训练；三是把动作专家从生成器中拆分出来，形成策略。
3）结果：作为世界模型，GreenWAM 在 WorldArena 1.0 上的轨迹、深度和3D精度都属顶级，超过对比中的世界-动作模型和视频生成器。作为策略，它在 RoboTwin 2.0 榜单名列前茅，在 LIBERO-plus 零样本成功率最高，在 CALVIN 和 LIBERO 上与专门的 VLA/世界-动作策略相当。迁移到真实人形机器人后，成功率高于由 π0.5 和 Cosmos 3 Edge 改造的策略，并可蒸馏成单步策略实现实时控制。
4）关键发现与意义：控制实验给出三条结论——按机器人特化能同时提升世界预测与控制；在适配早期就拆出动作专家更有帮助；策略适配时保留世界模型模式有助于应对场景变化。这说明“一个世界模型兼顾两种角色”是可行的，为跨机型通用机器人基础模型提供了可复制的训练范式。

rm.usage: 其“共享动作空间+世界-动作联合训练+拆分动作专家成策略”的配方可迁移到哨兵/多机策略的强化学习训练与sim-to-real，统一未来预测与策略生成，提升实车迁移鲁棒性。

items.title_en: EviScene: Beyond "Is It AI?" for Agentic Image Factuality Assessment
items.title_zh: EviScene：超越“是否为AI生成”的智能体式图像事实性评估
items.abstract_en: Determining whether an image is AI-generated does not establish whether the situation it depicts is factually supported. We formulate Image Factuality Assessment: given an image and a generic verification instruction, a system returns a supported or refuted verdict with an evidence-grounded explanation. Without a supplied textual claim, the system must progressively refine factual questions during investigation and align external evidence with the specific situation depicted. We introduce EviLens, an expert-reviewed benchmark of 10,174 supported and refuted images from controlled construction and web collection, covering twelve factual error types and evaluating both verdict accuracy and evidence sufficiency. We develop EviScene, a multimodal ReAct agent that interleaves visual inspection, external retrieval, and evidence analysis, using new findings to refine its questions and revisit relevant image details. We train a compact policy with supervised fine-tuning on reviewed teacher trajectories, followed by privileged on-policy self-distillation applied to verified decisions from the policy's own investigations. On the 1,527-image test set, the trained Qwen3.5-9B agent achieves 79.05% balanced accuracy and a Strict Evidence Sufficiency Rate (SESR) of 52.26%, improving over the same-backbone base agent by 6.71 and 9.37 percentage points, respectively. Its SESR is the highest among the evaluated agents.Code, models, and data will be released at https://github.com/wangzian828/EVISCENE and https://huggingface.co/ZiAnwang/EviScene.
items.abstract_zh: 判断一张图是否由AI生成，并不能说明它所描绘的情境是否有事实依据。我们提出“图像事实性评估”任务：给定一张图像和一条通用核查指令，系统需返回“支持”或“驳斥”的判定，并给出有证据支撑的解释。在没有给定文本主张的情况下，系统必须在调查过程中逐步细化事实问题，并将外部证据与图中具体情境对齐。我们提出 EviLens，一个经专家审阅的基准，包含来自受控构造与网络收集的10,174张支持与驳斥图像，覆盖12种事实错误类型，同时评估判定准确性与证据充分性。我们开发了 EviScene——一个多模态 ReAct 智能体，交替进行视觉检查、外部检索与证据分析，并利用新发现修正提问、重看相关图像细节。我们先用审阅过的教师轨迹做监督微调，再用特权在线自蒸馏，针对智能体自身调查中被验证的决策训练一个紧凑策略。在1,527张图像的测试集上，训练后的 Qwen3.5-9B 智能体达到79.05%的平衡准确率和52.26%的严格证据充分率（SESR），比同骨干基线智能体分别提升6.71和9.37个百分点，其 SESR 在所有被评估智能体中最高。代码、模型与数据将公开。
items.highlight_zh: 把图像核查从“是否AI生成”推进到“情境是否有事实依据”
items.digest_zh:
1）研究问题：判断一张图是不是AI生成的，并不能说明图中描绘的情境在现实中真有依据。作者提出“图像事实性评估”：给定一张图和一条通用核查指令，系统要给出“支持”或“驳斥”的结论，并附上有证据支撑的解释。难点在于没有现成文本主张，系统必须自己一步步细化问题，再把外部证据与图中具体情境对齐。
2）方法：构建 EviLens 基准，共10,174张来自受控构造与网络收集的支持/驳斥图像，覆盖12类事实错误，同时评估结论准确性与证据是否充分。提出 EviScene，一个多模态 ReAct 智能体，交替进行视觉检查、外部检索和证据分析，并用新发现反过来修正提问、回看图像细节。训练上，先用专家审阅过的教师轨迹做监督微调，再用特权在线自蒸馏，针对智能体自身调查中被验证的决策继续优化。
3）结果：在1,527张图的测试集上，训练后的 Qwen3.5-9B 智能体取得79.05%的平衡准确率和52.26%的严格证据充分率（SESR），比同骨干的基线智能体分别高出6.71和9.37个百分点，其 SESR 在被评估的智能体中最高。
4）意义：把“是不是AI图”升级为“图里的事有没有事实依据”，并给出可量化的证据充分性指标，为可信多模态核查提供了数据、方法与评测基准。

rm.usage: 图像事实性核查（支持/驳斥+证据）与自瞄、雷达、导航等赛事任务无关，基本用不上。

items.title_en: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
items.title_zh: Cepheid：面向跨几何族运动补全的尺度与结构解耦
items.abstract_en: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. Since this scale depends on unknown target motion, it cannot be measured directly at test time. We decouple residual structure from physical scale by learning a dimensionless prior, estimating amplitude from observables and a lightweight correction fitted only on training sources. Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/
items.abstract_zh: 稀疏到稠密的运动补全旨在从稀疏顶点位移恢复稠密网格运动。在某一几何族上训练的残差先验，一旦离开该族，往往打不过无需参数的调和延拓。此外，跨族训练还遇到尺度障碍：残差幅度在不同几何族间相差超过一个数量级，并且随观测变密而急剧缩小。由于该尺度取决于未知的目标运动，测试时无法直接测量。我们将残差结构与物理尺度解耦：学习一个无量纲先验来描述结构，从可观测量估计幅度，并加入一个仅在训练来源上拟合的轻量校正。我们的统一模型在所有评估过的几何族上都优于调和延拓，包括未见过的布料与足式身体，且无需骨架、配准或跨网格对应关系。同一先验无需重新训练即可用于点跟踪的动物视频，以及机器人抓取软体物体的场景。
items.highlight_zh: 解耦残差结构与物理尺度，实现跨几何族运动补全
items.digest_zh:
1）研究问题：如何从少量稀疏顶点位移，恢复出稠密的网格运动（稀疏到稠密运动补全）。作者指出两个痛点：在一个几何族上训练的残差先验，换到别的几何族时常常还不如完全无需参数的调和延拓；而跨族训练又撞上“尺度障碍”——不同几何族的残差幅度相差一个数量级以上，并且观测越密幅度越小。麻烦的是，这个尺度取决于未知的目标运动，测试时根本无法直接量出来。
2）方法：Cepheid 把残差的“结构”和“物理尺度”拆开处理：先学一个无量纲的先验，只描述残差的形状结构；尺度则从测试时可观测的量中估计，再加一个只在训练来源上拟合的轻量校正来补偿偏差。
3）结果：这个统一模型在评估过的所有几何族上都胜过调和延拓，包括训练中没见过的布料和足式身体，而且不需要骨架、配准或跨网格对应关系。同一个先验不用重新训练，就能直接用在点跟踪得到的动物视频上，也适用于机器人抓取软体物体的场景。
4）意义：它点出了一个被忽视却很根本的问题——残差幅度随几何族与观测密度剧烈变化，并给出可信的解耦方案，使运动补全模型真正具备跨族、跨域泛化能力。

rm.usage: 跨几何族的网格运动补全与软体抓取场景与比赛（装甲板识别、旋转能量机关、刚性能量单元装配）关联弱，基本用不上。

items.title_en: Data-Centric Recursive Self-Improvement for Navigation via Policy-Synchronized Language-Action Dual Bootstrapping
items.title_zh: 面向导航的数据中心式递归自我改进：通过策略同步的语言-动作双自举
items.abstract_en: Vision-language navigation requires agents to follow natural-language instructions to reach target locations, making high-quality language supervision essential. Since human annotation is costly, prior work has explored scalable data synthesis methods. However, existing methods typically either use separate models for navigation and instruction generation or couple the two tasks through task-specific components; most also annotate the full trajectory corpus with a fixed model before updating, which can cause generated supervision to lag behind the evolving policy. Therefore, we introduce RSI-Nav, a data-centric recursive self-improvement framework for navigation via policy-synchronized language-action dual bootstrapping, which unifies vision-language-to-action instruction following and vision-action-to-language instruction generation within a shared model. Specifically, after supervised fine-tuning establishes fundamental capabilities, RSI-Nav progressively processes unlabeled trajectories in small shards. The current model generates instructions for these trajectories, executes them to evaluate goal completion and path efficiency, retains qualified samples, and immediately updates itself before processing the next shard. This shard-wise update keeps newly generated supervision aligned with the evolving policy. We also incorporate spatial understanding data, since stronger spatial reasoning benefits navigation. Extensive experiments show that RSI-Nav reaches 68.6% SR on R2R-CE and 72.4% SR on RxR-CE, while providing stronger instruction-generation utility and modestly improved spatial understanding after recursive evolution.
items.abstract_zh: 视觉语言导航要求智能体按自然语言指令抵达目标位置，高质量语言监督因此至关重要。人工标注昂贵，已有可扩展合成方法要么用分离模型分别做导航与指令生成，要么用任务专用组件耦合两者；多数方法还用固定模型一次性标注整个轨迹语料再进行更新，使生成的监督滞后于策略演化。为此，我们提出 RSI-Nav——面向导航的数据中心式递归自我改进框架，通过策略同步的语言-动作双自举，在共享模型中统一「视觉-语言到动作」的指令跟随与「视觉-动作到语言」的指令生成。监督微调奠定基础能力后，RSI-Nav 以小块分片处理无标注轨迹：当前模型生成指令、执行以评估目标完成与路径效率、保留合格样本，并在处理下一片前立即自我更新，使新监督与策略同步。我们同时引入空间理解数据。实验表明，RSI-Nav 在 R2R-CE 上达到 68.6% 成功率，RxR-CE 上 72.4%，并带来更强的指令生成效用与适度提升的空间理解。
items.highlight_zh: 让语言监督与策略同步演化，R2R-CE 成功率 68.6%
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究了什么问题：视觉语言导航（VLN）要求智能体听懂自然语言指令并走到目标地点，所以「语言监督」的质量非常关键。人工标注太贵，已有自动合成方法有两大毛病：一是导航和指令生成用两个分开的模型，或者靠任务专用模块勉强耦合；二是先把整个轨迹库用一个固定模型标注完，再去更新策略，于是标注出来的监督总是「落后」于正在进化的策略。
2. 用了什么方法：作者提出 RSI-Nav，核心是「策略同步的语言-动作双自举」。它在同一个共享模型里同时做两件事：视觉+语言→动作（按指令走）和视觉+动作→语言（给轨迹写指令）。训练分两步：先用监督微调打好底子，然后把海量无标注轨迹切成小片（shard）逐片处理——当前模型先给这批轨迹生成指令，再执行这些指令，检查是否真的到达目标、路径是否高效，合格的样本留下用来自我更新，更新完才处理下一片。这样「新造出来的监督」和「刚刚更新过的策略」始终对得上。作者还额外加入空间理解数据，因为空间推理更强对导航有帮助。
3. 有什么结果：在 R2R-CE 基准上成功率达到 68.6%，RxR-CE 上达到 72.4%；经过这种递归演化后，模型写指令的能力也更强，空间理解有小幅提升。
4. 为何重要：它说明「边造数据边更新模型、让二者同步」比「一次性离线标注」更有效，也说明把指令生成与指令执行放进同一个模型可以互相促进，为可扩展的导航数据自举提供了一条实用路径。

rm.usage: “策略同步的语言-动作双自举、分片在线自我更新”的递归自我改进范式可迁移到哨兵导航/策略训练：自生成指令+执行验证筛选数据并即时更新策略，降低实车标注与调试成本。

items.title_en: WAVE-0: Bridging VLA Policies and WAMs with Lightweight Latent Future Prediction
items.title_zh: WAVE-0：以轻量隐未来预测桥接 VLA 策略与世界动作模型
items.abstract_en: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies excel at generalist robotic manipulation but generate actions without explicitly modeling their environmental consequences. World action models (WAMs) incorporate future prediction, yet most rely on costly video generation, while latent alternatives either use predicted futures only as auxiliary targets or infer latent actions from suboptimal visual transitions through costly large-scale video pretraining. We introduce WAVE-0 (World-model-Augmented VLA Execution), a framework that bridges VLAs and WAMs through a lightweight latent world model. By connecting the semantic understanding of pretrained VLAs with explicit future prediction, WAVE-0 allows anticipated action consequences to directly guide action generation. Built on a pretrained VLA, its 257M world model translates VLM-generated latent action plans into predicted future representations that condition the action expert, unifying latent planning, future prediction, and action generation. The world model is trained directly on ground-truth robot actions with a counterfactual ranking objective, requiring neither pixel reconstruction nor large-scale video pretraining. WAVE-0 achieves success rates of 91.47% on RoboTwin 2.0 and 98.7% on LIBERO, along with 88.0%, 61.4%, and 75.0% on LIBERO-Plus, LIBERO-Pro, and LIBERO-Para, respectively. On real-world tasks, it improves the success rate of $π_{0.5}$ from 38.3% to 73.3%. These results demonstrate strong manipulation performance and generalization across diverse distribution shifts.
items.abstract_zh: 视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略擅长通用机器人操作，但生成动作时并不显式建模其环境后果。世界动作模型（WAM）引入未来预测，但多数依赖昂贵的视频生成；基于隐空间的替代方案要么仅把预测未来当作辅助目标，要么需通过昂贵的大规模视频预训练，从次优的视觉转移中推断隐动作。我们提出 WAVE-0（世界模型增强的 VLA 执行），用一个轻量隐世界模型桥接 VLA 与 WAM。它把预训练 VLA 的语义理解与显式的未来预测相连，使预想的动作后果直接指导动作生成。其 2.57 亿参数的世界模型将 VLM 生成的隐动作计划转化为预测的未来表征，用以条件化动作专家，统一了隐规划、未来预测与动作生成。该世界模型直接以真值机器人动作、用反事实排序目标训练，无需像素重建或大规模视频预训练。WAVE-0 在 RoboTwin 2.0 上成功率 91.47%，LIBERO 上 98.7%，LIBERO-Plus、LIBERO-Pro、LIBERO-Para 上分别为 88.0%、61.4%、75.0%；在真实任务中把 π0.5 的成功率从 38.3% 提升到 73.3%，展现出强操作性能与跨分布偏移的泛化能力。
items.highlight_zh: 轻量隐世界模型让 VLA 预判动作后果，真机成功率近翻倍
items.digest_zh:
1. 研究了什么问题：视觉-语言-动作（VLA）策略是当下通用的机器人操作模型，但它只负责「看到、听懂、出动作」，并不显式思考「这个动作会让环境变成什么样」。世界动作模型（WAM）能预测未来，可大多靠生成视频来实现，代价昂贵；一些用隐空间代替视频的做法，要么只把预测的未来当作训练时的辅助任务，并不真正用它来指导出动作，要么必须靠大规模视频预训练，从质量并不理想的视觉变化里反推隐动作，成本同样很高。
2. 用了什么方法：作者提出 WAVE-0（World-model-Augmented VLA Execution）。做法是在一个预训练 VLA 之上外挂一个仅 2.57 亿参数的轻量隐世界模型：VLM 先给出隐动作计划，这个世界模型把计划翻译成「未来会变成什么样」的表征，再用这个未来表征去条件化动作专家（action expert），也就是让「预想的后果」直接参与动作生成。由此，隐规划、未来预测、动作生成被统一在一个框架里。训练上，世界模型直接拿真值机器人动作做监督，用反事实排序（counterfactual ranking）目标学习，既不需要重建像素，也不需要跑大规模视频预训练，训练成本大幅下降。
3. 有什么结果：在仿真基准 RoboTwin 2.0 上成功率 91.47%，LIBERO 上 98.7%；在更难的分布偏移版本 LIBERO-Plus、LIBERO-Pro、LIBERO-Para 上分别为 88.0%、61.4%、75.0%。真实世界任务中，把 π0.5 的成功率从 38.3% 提升到 73.3%，几乎翻倍。
4. 为何重要：它证明了「让机器人先在心里预演一下后果」并不一定要付出视频生成或大规模视频预训练的代价——一个轻量隐空间世界模型就够了，而且能同时提升操作能力和对分布变化的泛化性，为 VLA 与世界模型的结合提供了一条低成本、可扩展的路线。

rm.usage: 用轻量隐世界模型增强VLA动作生成的思路可参考到工程视觉装配的机械臂策略，以及哨兵自主交火/走位的RL训练，通过预测动作后果提升跨分布鲁棒性。

items.title_en: Open-o3-Video-v2: Seek, Ground, and Reason with Verifiable Spatio-Temporal Evidence
items.title_zh: Open-o3-Video-v2：基于可验证时空证据的寻找、定位与推理
items.abstract_en: Reliable video reasoning requires models to produce correct answers and expose supporting visual evidence. Open-o3-Video enables verifiable reasoning by embedding timestamps and object-level bounding boxes into reasoning traces, but is restricted to frames from an initial sparse sampler. We introduce Open-o3-Video-v2, which formulates video reasoning as a unified agentic evidencegrounded process. The model identifies missing information, acquires additional observations, grounds the moments and objects supporting its reasoning, and writes this evidence into the trajectory before continuing or answering. To support this behavior, we construct STGR-v2-CoT135K, including 52K multi-turn agentic grounded reasoning trajectories, and STGR-v2-RL-13K for reinforcement learning. We further propose Clue-Seek GRPO (CS-GRPO), which tracks how tool calls change accumulated evidence, rewards clue coverage and step-wise gains, and penalizes excessive, repetitive, or uninformative retrieval. On V-STaR, Open-o3-Video-v2-4B achieves 40.4% mAM and 56.3% mLGM, outperforming its Qwen3-VL-4B backbone by 8.5% and 12.6%, respectively. It also delivers consistent gains across general video understanding, long-video reasoning, and temporal grounding benchmarks. These results show that active evidence acquisition and verifiable object-level grounding are complementary for reliable video reasoning. The code and models are released at https://msalab-pku.github.io/projects/Open-o3-Video-v2.
items.comment: Extension of Open-o3-Video (https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.20579). V2 extends single-pass grounded reasoning to agentic multi-turn evidence seeking and grounding, enabling models to actively acquire and reason over missing visual evidence. We further introduce STGR-v2-CoT-135K and CS-GRPO to improve evidence acquisition and grounded reasoning

items.title_en: WorldRecon: Generative Multi-View Mesh Reconstruction for Large-Scale 3D World
items.title_zh: WorldRecon：面向大规模3D世界的生成式多视图网格重建
items.abstract_en: Reconstructing complete, high-quality meshes of large-scale scenes from unposed multi-view images requires faithful geometric grounding while plausibly completing surfaces that are unobserved or only sparsely captured. We present WorldRecon, a generative multi-view reconstruction framework for recovering complete, large-scale 3D scene meshes from unposed RGB images. WorldRecon uses a coarse, noisy global point cloud and camera poses estimated from the input images by a reconstruction model as a global scaffold for whole-scene generation and partitions it into overlapping spatial blocks. To robustly leverage these imperfect geometric priors, we equip the native 3D generative model TRELLIS.2 with a dedicated reconstruction-based conditioning architecture that generates each block from its local point-cloud crop and block-relevant image observations, producing sparse structure, detailed geometry, and PBR materials. To maintain scene-level coherence, we introduce neighbour-aware latent inpainting and a causal world-generation procedure that propagates structural, geometric, and material context across overlapping blocks. Together, these designs scale multi-view generative reconstruction to large-scale scenes, yielding coherent, unified meshes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that WorldRecon achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction performance, reducing Chamfer distance by 14.9% and 43.1% while improving F-score by 17.3% and 12.0% over the strongest baselines on synthetic and real-world indoor scenes, respectively, thereby demonstrating faithful and complete generative reconstruction as well as strong sim-to-real generalization. Project page: https://kszpxxzmc.github.io/WorldRecon-website/.

items.title_en: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models
items.title_zh: ACCRUE：面向机器人基础模型的持续离策略强化学习
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. Existing continual RL methods on top of VLAs mitigate forgetting but rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, whereas off-policy methods improve single-task sample efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. The inherited critic adapts only on current-task transitions and guides current-task actor learning, while prior behavior is preserved by distilling the actor toward cached targets on a small number of retained episodes. Fixed visual features keep the inherited learner and its replay compatible with base-policy updates. Across contact-rich assembly sequences in simulation and on real-robot hardware, ACCRUE accelerates subsequent-task learning with near-zero forgetting and significantly reduces real-robot training time by 31.0\% to 68.5\%.

rm.usage: 持续离策略强化学习框架可保留跨任务学到的行为，适合在仿真/实车中分阶段训练哨兵自瞄交火、走位策略而不遗忘旧技能，用于团队策略的持续迭代。

items.title_en: PACT: Posture-Aligned Co-Design Technique for Hand Configuration and Retargeting in Multi-Finger Imitation Learning
items.title_zh: PACT：用于多指模仿学习中手部构型与重定向的姿态对齐协同设计技术
items.abstract_en: The fidelity of teleoperated demonstrations used for imitation learning is determined by how faithfully a robot hand can replicate the operator's posture. The posture retargeting law that the robot will execute is typically selected only once the hardware has been finalized, and conventional hand designs often neglect human-like grasping postures. We introduce PACT, an optimization based on human grasping postures that jointly optimizes the mechanical parameters of a 17-servo robot hand (link lengths, joint offsets, mounting angles, and base placements) and its nonlinear posture retargeter (a linear human-to-robot joint map, per-joint posture-IK weights, and damping). The optimization enforces full-finger correspondence (MCP, PIP, DIP, and tip of each finger) to human poses from the DexYCB dataset, and is constrained by servo interference, assembly clearances, and flat-hand protrusion, so the resulting design can be physically assembled. We fabricate the PACT Hand and validate it through teleoperation experiments and an imitation-learning demonstration. The hand reproduces all human hand keypoints with a kinematic RMSE of 3.9 mm, compared to 12.8 mm for the LEAP Hand baseline, and keeps all fingertips within 10 mm on every grasping posture, while the baseline achieves this for only 21.6% of the poses. Under matched per-joint torque limits, it lifts twice the baseline payload, 2 kg against 1 kg, and deforms a held paper cup seven times less, reaching a deformation level comparable to a human hand. It also achieves an 86% grasping success rate on YCB daily objects, compared to 64% for the baseline. Finally, as a demonstration, an imitation-learning policy trained on demonstrations collected with the PACT Hand achieved a 75% success rate at held-out placements in a can pick-and-place task. Project page: https://pact-hand-2027.github.io
items.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027. Project page: https://pact-hand-2027.github.io

items.title_en: Intent-guided Adaptive Stiffening for Visuomotor Policies under Unknown Resistance
items.title_zh: 面向未知阻力下视觉运动策略的意图引导自适应刚度增强
items.abstract_en: Manipulation tasks such as unscrewing a cap or sliding a part in contact with a surface require imposing force along a high-friction direction: the robot must overcome a resistance rather than yield to it. Generative visuomotor policies predict the motion for such tasks but not the authority needed to realize it, and that authority is bounded by the impedance controller beneath them: when the resistance exceeds what a compliant controller can exert under a bounded tracking error, the task is unattainable however accurate the prediction is. The required amount cannot be anticipated either, since it depends on a contact state the observation does not reveal. In this paper, we propose a residual stiffening layer placed underneath an unmodified policy. Resistance is recognized, without force sensing, from the mismatch between the motion the policy commands and the motion the robot realizes, and a four-mode supervisor raises the stiffness along a single direction read off the policy's own action chunk, retains it while the task progresses and releases it afterwards. The layer needs no compliance labels, no retraining and no re-collected demonstrations. On two real tasks, unscrewing a bottle cap and pushing a T-nut along a T-slot groove against non-homogeneous friction, evaluated at six resistance levels of which two were withheld from the demonstrations, the layer raises the success rate from 52% to 90% while producing 61% less peak off-axis force than a uniformly stiff controller at the same resistance.

items.title_en: Mobility-Budget-Constrained Submodular Maximization for Distributed Semantic Multi-Robot Exploration
items.title_zh: 面向分布式语义多机器人探索的移动预算约束次模最大化
items.abstract_en: Multi-robot exploration under communication and mobility constraints requires balancing information gain with reachability. We present a distributed semantic exploration framework that combines Dirichlet mapping, budget-constrained trajectory selection, and Resource-Aware distributed Greedy (RAG) coordination. Each robot clusters frontiers, computes terrain- and heading-aware least-cost paths with a single budget-limited Dijkstra search, and selects feasible paths by marginal information gain, represented by the expected reduction in Dirichlet entropy. Each robot's per-round selection is exact, the team's joint per-round information gain is at least half the centralized optimum, and the bound degrades gracefully under limited communication. Ten-run gridworld ablations show improved coverage, semantic mIoU, and map certainty with lower entropy and traversal cost per unit distance than shortest-distance frontier selection. Budget-sensitivity experiments show that an intermediate budget best balances path reach and receding-horizon execution. In photorealistic full-system simulation against five coordination rules run in their native published forms, the proposed method attains the highest mean coverage and semantic accuracy while being the only one that respects the per-trajectory mobility budget.
items.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures. Accepted to the IROS 2026 SeMaNa Workshop. The first two authors contributed equally

items.title_en: Improving Policy Learning from Delayed Interventions
items.title_zh: 改进基于延迟干预的策略学习
items.abstract_en: In this work, we explore the idea of expert intervention delays in human-supervised robotic systems for imitation learning system. Previous works in imitation learning have primarily examined the impact of suboptimal experts, where the expert policy makes mistakes, but assumed expert interventions occur immediately after errors are made. Although delayed expert intervention can be viewed as a form of noise that might improve policy robustness, our results show that learning from delayed expert interventions is overall less effective than learning from non-delayed expert interventions; delayed expert interventions are less effective at demonstrating error avoidance behaviors. To address this, we propose Learning from Delayed Intervention (LfDI), which learns a cost function based on where and when the expert intervenes, combined with limited information about the extent of intervention delays provided by the expert. This cost function is then used to infer additional supervision for states without expert data, guiding the policy to avoid states that would likely trigger interventions. We evaluate our method, Learning from Delayed Intervention (LfDI), on simulated environments and show that it outperforms other methods that do not account for intervention delays.

rm.usage: 分析延迟干预对模仿学习的影响，可用于理解人类遥操作标注（如示范哨兵走位/自瞄策略）时延带来的训练退化，指导策略学习数据采集流程。

items.title_en: MSC: Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control Framework with Uncertainty-Aware NMPC and RL-based Execution Layer
items.title_zh: MSC：具有不确定性感知NMPC与基于RL执行层的多阶段连铸机感知控制框架
items.abstract_en: Freely swiveling casters are widely adopted in industrial AMRs/SDVs for their mechanical simplicity and load capacity. However, caster misalignment during low-speed or high-curvature maneuvers induces strong contact nonlinearities, widening the planning-execution gap between commanded $(v, ω)$ and realized motion. Existing caster-aware strategies are highly sensitive to state-estimation reliability, causing unstable execution in uncertain transition regimes. To address this, we present Multi-Stage Caster-aware Control (MSC), a planning-execution integrated hierarchical framework featuring two core mechanisms. First, an uncertainty-aware NMPC (CU-MPC) dynamically schedules caster-aware costs and input regularization using predictive uncertainty to suppress overly aggressive maneuvers. Second, a reinforcement learning-based execution layer estimates and predicts caster states under partial observability, transforming high-level velocity commands into physically executable wheel speeds adapted to current contact conditions. Validations in Isaac Sim and real robots demonstrate that MSC offers a clear comparative advantage over existing decoupled compensation approaches by significantly improving caster-state estimation accuracy, minimizing misalignment, and enhancing tracking robustness in caster-sensitive maneuvers.

items.title_en: All-St3R SLAM: Real-time RGB Dynamic SLAM with Pixel-wise Motion Masking
items.title_zh: All-St3R SLAM：具有像素级运动掩码的实时RGB动态SLAM
items.abstract_en: SLAM (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) is a core technology in autonomous systems that enables them to estimate their own position and build a map of unknown environments simultaneously. SLAM systems in dynamic environments are of great practical importance. However, existing dynamic SLAM approaches still have several limitations like over-removal and high computational costs. To address these limitations, we propose a real-time RGB Dynamic SLAM framework that precisely removes moving objects at the pixel level without relying on predefined labels or segmentation models. Our system combines pixel motion predicted by ego-motion using DUSt3R with point tracking from All-Tracker, removing only actually moving pixels by analyzing discrepancies between the two motion sources. Unlike object-level masking methods, our approach eliminates only currently moving regions, allowing temporarily static parts to be utilized for tracking. Operating at approximately 10 FPS, the system achieves real-time performance on standard 30 FPS video streams by subsampling every 3 frames. Relying solely on RGB inputs, this significantly improves upon state-of-the-art dense dynamic SLAM approaches (0.5-3 FPS), presenting a highly practical solution.
items.comment: Accepted to the IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS) 2026. Project Page: https://yellowon0103.github.io/all-st3r-slam/

items.title_en: UniW(A)M: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Framework for World and World-Action Models
items.title_zh: UniW(A)M：面向世界模型与世界-动作模型的统一专家混合框架
items.abstract_en: World models (WMs) and world-action models (WAMs) focus on future world prediction and executable action generation, respectively. Although these models learn shared physical dynamics and interaction semantics from embodied trajectories, they are typically trained in isolation, which restricts knowledge reuse between prediction and control. The central challenge is therefore to develop a unified learning framework that shares these dynamics while preserving the distinct modeling capabilities required by each paradigm. We propose UniW(A)M, a mixture-of-experts world-(action) model built upon diffusion Transformers that unifies action-conditioned world modeling and diverse WAM variants. Shared experts capture common dynamics, while atomic capability experts are reused across interfaces so that each interface keeps its own conditional pathway. At deployment, a plug-in adaptive interface router (PAIR) learns from a small subset of target-task chunk scenarios to select a suitable WAM interface for each execution chunk, balancing task success and execution efficiency while keeping the backbone frozen. We evaluate UniW(A)M on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and three real-world manipulation tasks, where it achieves 88.3% average real-world success versus 76.7% for the strongest baseline. On WorldArena, it leads action-conditioned world modeling on all three tasks. AC-WM co-training contributes to action generation on every action interface and PAIR raises OOD success from 63.3% to 76.7%.
items.comment: Under review at ICLR 2027. 34 pages, 19 figures, 15 tables

items.title_en: REFLEX: A Learned On-Board Reflex for Robust Autonomous Collision Recovery of Soft Quadrotors
items.title_zh: REFLEX：用于软体四旋翼鲁棒自主碰撞恢复的学习型机载反射
items.abstract_en: Collision-resilient airframes allow quadrotors to survive impacts, but do not ensure autonomous post-collision recovery. Innovation gating in stock onboard estimators often rejects valid external velocity measurements after high-speed impacts, compromising recovery. We present REFLEX, a collision-recovery flight mode that runs entirely on the flight controller, requiring neither contact sensors nor a companion computer. Its proprioceptive recurrent policy stabilizes the vehicle without position, velocity, heading, or altitude estimates. The translational estimate is reinitialized while REFLEX is active, and a trust gate checks estimator consistency before returning control to the stock autopilot. The policy is trained in simulation using proximal policy optimization, with episodes initialized from post-impact states measured in 47 real collisions. In hardware experiments, REFLEX recovered 19 of 22 wall impacts at 5.03 $\pm$ 0.09 m/s, compared with 1 of 14 for the matched stock autopilot. These included 15 consecutive recoveries in a single flight. A separate exploratory flight demonstrated two additional recoveries at 6.02 and 6.05 m/s within the same flight, exceeding the previously reported velocity for autonomous wall-collision recovery by 64%.

items.title_en: Enabling Token-wise Importance Sampling in Off-Policy RLVR with Proximal KL Regularization
items.title_zh: 在具有近端KL正则化的离策略RLVR中实现词元级重要性采样
items.abstract_en: Off-policy data in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can arise from asynchronous generation, rollout-training mismatch, and response reuse. Token-wise importance weighting avoids multiplying likelihood ratios across a response but generally biases policy gradients. We prove that, under coverage and local expressiveness conditions, full future KL credit makes the exact proximal optimizer the update's unique stationary policy, even for mixtures of older policies, without full-response weights or a fitted critic. We further establish convergence of continuous-time tabular population updates under persistent coverage and time-varying behavior policies, and a finite-sample reward guarantee for linear logistic models under additional assumptions. These results motivate Proximal KL, a practical off-policy RLVR method that separates the proximal reference from the sampling policy and replaces PPO clipping with bounded future KL credit. Across all seven matched off-policy comparisons on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B, spanning two learning rates, response reuse, and rollout staleness, Proximal KL outperforms GRPO in micro-averaged accuracy over eight math benchmarks by up to 2.58%. A separate on-policy comparison yields comparable aggregate accuracy. In periodic-refresh experiments, Proximal KL avoids the collapses observed in PG and CISPO, exceeds GRPO's training accuracy, and reaches higher accuracy in fewer policy updates. Ablations show that token-wise correction outperforms sequence-level and unweighted controls. With token-wise correction retained, future KL feedback reduces sensitivity to the tested baseline perturbation relative to PPO clipping. A finite future horizon improves AIME24 mean@16 and pass@16 over the full tail, while fixed-policy measurements show that truncation reduces correction variance over the tested horizons.

items.title_en: Can an Agent Learn to Predict Its Own Failure? Outcome-Grounded Confidence Calibration in LLM Agents
items.title_zh: 智能体能否学会预测自身失败？LLM 智能体中基于结果锚定的置信度校准
items.abstract_en: Controlling an acting LLM agent means deciding, at each step of a long-horizon task, whether to trust its next action, abstain, or hand off to a human. That decision needs a per-step confidence signal predicting whether the current rollout will eventually succeed. The agent's own self-reported verbalized confidence is the natural candidate, but existing reinforcement learning methods calibrate it against the correctness of a decision at the current step. We propose a method to calibrate it against the eventual outcome of a multi-step episode: under GRPO, the group of rollouts for a task supplies success labels, and a proper scoring rule scores each step's confidence against the realized outcome. In offline RL on recorded trajectories of a Qwen2.5-7B agent in ALFWorld, TextWorld, and WebShop environments, the AUROC of step confidence against episode outcome rises from near chance to 0.68-0.85, and the top-10% of steps the agent is most confident about succeed ~4.3x more often than average. In online RL on the live ALFWorld agent, four calibration rewards improve early-step AUROC, expected calibration error goes from 0.42 to below 0.12, and selective execution improves over both the untrained agent and a format-only RL control, without degrading task success. We also introduce an evaluation protocol that separates episode depth, task difficulty, and attempt-level foresight, which shows where the gain lies: the trained agent recognizes from its first step which tasks it will fail, while telling a succeeding attempt from a failing one at the same task is harder, with some early-window signal emerging on TextWorld.

rm.usage: 让智能体按整局最终成败校准每步置信度，可借思路判断哨兵自主决策是否该继续执行还是切换/回传，但原方法针对 LLM 长程任务，需大改。

items.title_en: Let the Mind Conceive, Let the Hand Achieve: Following Multimodal Instructions for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation
items.title_zh: 让心智构想，让手去实现：遵循多模态指令的长时程机器人操作
items.abstract_en: A robot following a multi-step instruction needs to act on the right objects in the right order, even as the scene changes. It must also maintain awareness of task progress and determine when to advance. To address these challenges, we introduce Orchestra, an agent harness that separates task planning and execution management from action generation. Orchestra decomposes a complete multimodal instruction into ordered subtasks, tracks completed steps, and updates the locations of relevant objects and destinations during execution. It maintains a shared context containing the active subtask, spatial grounding, and recent observations. An action policy uses this context to generate actions, while a separately trained progress evaluator estimates when to advance to the next subtask. To evaluate whether robots trained on atomic instructions and short trajectories can execute longer subtask sequences, we introduce a benchmark named RMBench-Compose. Orchestra achieves a mean success rate of $68.22\%$ across nine RMBench tasks, outperforming Mem-0 by $26.22$ percentage points. On RMBench-Compose, it achieves an Average Success Length (ASL) of $7.35$ subtasks, $2.46$ times that of HarnessVLA. Across four real-world multi-step tasks, it improves mean ASL by $25.0\%$ over Orchestra using the base $π_{0.5}$ policy. These results show that Orchestra helps robots carry out longer sequences of subtasks while preserving the requested subtask order and acting on the specified objects. Our code and project page are available at https://youpengwen.github.io/Orchestra.

items.title_en: Smoothness Ranks Skill, Not Success: An Audit of Published Trajectory-Smoothness Curation Metrics Under Episode-Length Controls
items.title_zh: 平滑度衡量的是技能，而非成功：对已发表轨迹平滑度筛选指标在回合长度控制下的审计
items.abstract_en: Trajectory smoothness has been proposed as a cheap, training-free signal for curating imitation-learning demonstrations, most recently by rinse, which introduces Spectral Arc Length (SAL) and a contact-aware Trajectory-Envelope Distance (TED). We test whether these published metrics survive episode-length controls on real robomimic data. On can/mh, SAL separates better from worse operators with AUROC 0.952, but episode length alone achieves 0.957, and inside a duration-matched band SAL falls to 0.628 while raw mean jerk, the baseline rinse argues against, rises to 0.896. The confound replicates on square/mh. On can/mg, where every episode is exactly 150 steps, SAL is at chance (0.454) and TED is inverted (0.376) against task success, while jerk reaches 0.706. Training GMM behavior-cloning policies on each metric's curated subset (10 seeds), curating by TED costs roughly a third of downstream success relative to random selection of the same size (0.240 vs. 0.360, p=0.0001, surviving Bonferroni correction), while SAL and jerk are indistinguishable from not curating. Under a diffusion policy TED still ranks worst, though its deficit is not resolvable at five seeds, and jerk becomes significantly better than both baselines, so the curation decision does not transfer unchanged across the two policy configurations we tested. Inspecting trajectories shows why TED inverts: successful manipulation requires sustained high-deviation motion through contact, while failure is low-amplitude hovering that a smoothed envelope follows closely.
items.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures. Accepted (poster) at the NeurIPS 2026 RoboPAD Workshop. Code: https://github.com/imjbassi/smoothness-metric-audit

items.title_en: Position: Beyond Training Time, Test-Time Coordination is Essential for Cooperative MARL
items.title_zh: 立场：超越训练时——测试时协调对合作式 MARL 至关重要
items.abstract_en: We argue that cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) should treat test-time coordination as part of the problem definition rather than a deployment artifact. Our focus is on long-horizon, centrally monitored cooperative systems such as warehouse robotics, automated storage-and-retrieval systems, and cloud-resource scheduling, where teams share a reward, operate under shifting objectives, and already run with global telemetry at deployment. The dominant paradigm in this regime, centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE), uses global information only during training and provides no coordination channel at execution. This is sufficient when agents are weakly coupled or the environment is stationary, but it fails when the team must realign after conditions change. The limitation is structural rather than algorithmic, and more training cannot add a channel that does not exist at execution time. We call this the recoverability gap. To address it, we name the underexplored design space of intermittent test-time coordination as centralized training with mixed execution (CTME), in which a coordinator observes global state and emits high-level signals while agents act locally. CTME is not a particular learning algorithm, but a cooperative MARL problem setting that makes test-time information structure explicit. It specifies team-level information, high-level signals, and update frequency after training, with CTDE recovered as a limit case. We do not argue that CTDE is obsolete. We argue that removing the test-time channel is a modeling choice, not a necessity, and the wrong default when global telemetry is available and teams must recover from drift.

items.title_en: 3D-VITAL: Visibility-aware Identity Training from Artificial Liftings of 3D Reconstruction model for Cross-View Object Re-Identification
items.title_zh: 3D-VITAL：基于 3D 重建模型人工提升的可见性感知身份训练用于跨视角物体重识别
items.abstract_en: We address the Cross-View Object Re-Identification (ReID) task, aiming to match identities across drastically different viewpoints. We focus on Single-View Aerial-Ground ReID (SV AG-ReID), where models train on one viewpoint and must generalize to another at inference. To bridge this viewpoint gap, related work employs generative models to synthesize novel views from source images as additional training data. We leverage recent advances in large-scale single-view 3D mesh reconstruction to lift source images into textured meshes and to render them from new viewpoints. However, this pipeline produces unreliable data in two distinct ways. First, the reconstruction may fail and produce geometrically incorrect meshes, resulting in severe corruption in rendered novel views. Second, even when the geometry is correct, the rendered novel views contain hallucinated textures in regions not visible in the source image. The reconstructed mesh carries a per-pixel partition between regions visible from the source view and regions that the reconstruction model had to hallucinate, available as a deterministic byproduct of rendering. We introduce this per-pixel visibility map and exploit it in a two-stage design. Cross-View Consistency Filtering (CVCF) discards geometrically incorrect meshes by ensuring multi-view consistency between source and novel views over visible patches. Visibility-Aware Attention Supervision (VAAS) leverages the visibility map to guide the model's attention toward reliable regions of the rendered view during training. Combined, these two components enable our method, 3D-VITAL, to better leverage the synthetic signal from single-view 3D mesh reconstruction. 3D-VITAL sets a new state-of-the-art on three SV AG-ReID benchmarks. Code and data will be released at https://github.com/TurtleSmoke/3D-VITAL.

rm.usage: 跨视角物体重识别可用 3D 重建生成新视角训练数据，有助于雷达多相机覆盖下对敌方机器人的跨视角身份匹配与持续标记。

items.title_en: What Limits Cross-Task Generalization in World Action Models?
items.title_zh: 是什么限制了世界动作模型中的跨任务泛化？
items.abstract_en: Cross-task generalization remains difficult for world action models (WAMs), even when their predicted futures depict plausible manipulation. This gap can be attributed directly: we make this gap directly testable by decoupling a WAM into a world model and an inverse-dynamics model (IDM), then holding the IDM fixed while replacing the source of future images. We introduce Align Once, Evaluate Everywhere (AoE), a camera-space inverse-dynamics model pretrained on large-scale robot data, which provides this recovery interface for different future sources across tasks and environments. Through it, we find that actions recovered from recorded futures of unseen tasks execute almost as well as replayed demonstrations, whereas futures predicted by world models collapse across benchmarks. The failures are not generic: they concentrate on the gripper and interaction geometry while generation capacity is spent on task-irrelevant background. This diagnosis suggests that supervision should target exactly these regions. We therefore introduce the vision-to-action (VITA) loss, which passes generated futures through the frozen AoE and penalizes discrepancies in the recovered actions, redirecting generation toward action-relevant detail. Across two world models and three manipulation benchmarks, this simple change raises the execution success of generated futures from near zero to 47.0%. The same loss also transfers to WAMs and yields consistent gains in native control.
items.comment: 34 pages, 10 figures, under review in ICLR 2027

items.title_en: AeroChem: Closed-loop Physics-Informed State Space Modeling for Long-term Chemically-Reactive Air Quality Forecasting--Extended Version
items.title_zh: AeroChem：面向长期化学反应性空气质量预报的闭环物理信息状态空间建模——扩展版
items.abstract_en: Accurate long-term air quality forecasting is challenging due to long-range transport, meteorological variability, and nonlinear chemical reactions underlying secondary pollutant formation. Purely data-driven models often suffer from long-horizon drift and lack physical consistency, while existing physics-informed approaches commonly follow open-loop designs that fuse neural and physical components only at the output level. We propose AeroChem, a closed-loop physics-informed state space framework for chemically reactive air quality forecasting. AeroChem adopts a two-branch co-correction design: a UDE-based process branch provides a structured but imperfect physical prior, while a Mamba-based virtual measurement branch captures long-range temporal context and produces probabilistic virtual observations. Neural Kalman Fusion couples the two branches by correcting the latent physical state at each forecasting step and feeding the posterior state back into the simulator, reducing long-horizon drift. We further introduce HanoiAir, a real-world dataset integrating pollutant concentrations, meteorology, and emission inventories. Experiments on HanoiAir and a public benchmark show that AeroChem improves long-horizon stability and sudden-change forecasting.
items.comment: 25 pages. An extended version of "AeroChem: Closed-loop Physics-Informed State Space Modeling for Long-term Chemically-Reactive Air Quality Forecasting--Extended Version" accepted at NeurIPS 2026

items.title_en: RoboBugBench: Benchmarking Automated Repair of Real Robot Software Under an Audited Behavioral Oracle
items.title_zh: RoboBugBench：在受审计行为预言机下对真实机器人软件自动修复的基准测试
items.abstract_en: Language agents increasingly modify robot software, but whether they can repair it is unmeasured, because the domain supplies no oracle to inherit: a robot bug manifests as behavior, and robot repositories ship almost no tests that capture it. We present RoboBugBench, a benchmark of 33 real, execution-validated defects in a pinned ROS 2 navigation stack, in which a candidate patch is graded by compiling it and driving the robot through a physics simulation rather than by running a unit test. Three frontier models, each given 1 attempt per instance, repair 24.2%-36.4%, with no pairwise difference significant; difficulty tracks the oracle rather than the domain, at 66.7% on instances graded by process survival against 22.2% on those graded by what the robot did (instance-level p = 0.0027). Because the oracle is constructed rather than inherited we audit it adversarially, and report the decomposition that audit yields: counterfeit patches which suppress a failure without repairing the defect are accepted by the shipped rule 11/11, while a distributional rule over the same data rejects 4 at no cost in false rejects. The residual is an observability bound (what the observation channel discards, no predicate over it can recover), so discrimination must be bought with instrumentation rather than stricter criteria, and our repair rates are bounds: inflated by what the oracle cannot distinguish, deflated by unanimity's rejection of correct fixes under run-to-run noise. We release the corpus, criterion batteries, counterfeit suite and cached telemetry.
items.comment: 14 pages: 9 main + references + two appendices. 1 figure, 4 tables. Accepted non-archival workshop paper at the Verify-Agents workshop ('Who Verifies the Agents?') at NeurIPS 2026, Sydney, Dec 11-12, 2026

items.title_en: Scaling Latent Motor Adaptation to Coordinated Bimanual Manipulation
items.title_zh: 将潜在运动自适应扩展到协调双臂操作
items.abstract_en: Robust manipulation under uncertain object dynamics and geometry remains a core challenge in real-world robotics. Policies trained under fixed assumptions often degrade when object mass, friction, scale, or shape vary. Embedding-based adaptation methods such as Rapid Motor Adaptation (RMA) address this by conditioning actions on latent representations of environment dynamics inferred from interaction history. We investigate whether this paradigm scales from single arm settings to coordinated bimanual manipulation, where higher dimensional control, coupled contacts, and shared object forces introduce additional complexity. We evaluate bimanual RMA on three contact-rich ManiSkill tasks with randomized YCB object properties. Bimanual RMA, using observation-action history and dual wrist depth images, retains privileged policy performance on bimanual picking and lifting, while an otherwise matched stationary PPO policy without latent conditioning achieves low success; all methods remain limited on long-horizon stacking. We further demonstrate direct sim-to-real transfer on a dual Franka lifting task without real-world finetuning. Together, these results suggest that latent conditioning provides useful structure for scaling robust control to coordinated bimanual systems, while longer horizon tasks require additional temporal structure.
items.comment: Accepted at the IROS 2026 Bimanual Manipulation Workshop. 5 pages, 4 figures

items.title_en: EventLens: Event-Structure Reinforcement Learning for Video Understanding
items.title_zh: EventLens：面向视频理解的事件结构强化学习
items.abstract_en: Recent multimodal large language models (MLLMs) achieve strong results on video question answering, yet often fail to recover the temporal structure that makes a video coherent. They may merge neighboring events, miss single-event progression, or infer implausible relations across events. We study structured temporal understanding as the ability to recover event structure from visual evidence, including event boundaries, single-event progression, and multi-event relations. We argue that this gap arises from a mismatch between current post-training objectives and temporal reasoning, where caption-style supervision allows models to rely on language shortcuts rather than visual temporal grounding. To address this, we propose EventLens, a vision-centric reinforcement learning framework that learns video understanding through event-structure recovery. Instead of reconstructing captions, EventLens trains models to recover temporal structure under controlled perturbations, such as altered temporal granularity, reversed progression, and shuffled event order. We instantiate this framework with a three-level temporal ontology and derive three verifiable task families: event segmentation, progression discrimination, and multi-event relation reasoning. These tasks admit deterministic rewards, enabling task-specialized GRPO training without human preference labels or learned reward models. We further introduce multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MT-OPD) to consolidate specialized policies into a unified model. Experiments on Qwen3-VL backbones show consistent improvements on temporal grounding and event-sensitive reasoning benchmarks, while preserving general video-QA performance. Learning curves further demonstrate that EventLens achieves comparable downstream transfer with significantly reduced training cost compared to direct mixed RL optimization.
items.comment: 22 pages, 8 figures, 13 tables. Project page: https://lostgreen.github.io/EventLens/

items.title_en: Shared-Control Teleoperation of Omnidirectional Aerial Robots for Continuous Valve Rotation
items.title_zh: 面向连续阀门旋转的全向空中机器人共享控制遥操作
items.abstract_en: Omnidirectional aerial robots offer full 6-DoF independent control over position and orientation, making them popular for aerial manipulation. Although there have been advancements in robotic autonomy, human operation remains essential in complex aerial environments. Previously, we proposed an aerial teleoperation system that brings the rotational flexibility of human hands into the unbounded aerial workspace, which was evaluated through a vertically mounted valve-turning task. However, due to the limited range of human forearm's motion, the robot could not continuously rotate the valve, hindering its application in industry. In this work, we propose an approach to initiate continuous rotation when the forearm angle exceeds a threshold. This switch of control authority exemplifies the concept shared control from human-robot interaction, marking a further step in aerial teleoperation.

items.title_en: Observation-Referenced Tissue Deformation Forecasting with Tool-Driven and Residual Dynamics
items.title_zh: 基于观察参考的组织变形预测：结合工具驱动动力学与残差动力学
items.abstract_en: Forecasting tissue deformation from future instrument motion could support predictive planning and increasingly autonomous surgical systems. We study this problem using a scene-specific differentiable surface model fitted to an observed tool-tissue interaction window. Rather than forecasting absolute simulated positions, we introduce an \textit{observation-referenced} formulation that anchors each tissue point to its last valid observation and adds only the deformation induced by the known, preplanned future tool trajectory. This reduces sensitivity to reconstruction, initialization, and persistent simulation offsets while preserving the predicted deformation response. The physical model uses differentiable, mesh-free position-based dynamics with scene-specific rigidity, attachment, region scale, and grasp coupling. We further introduce an optional \textit{observation-referenced residual model} combining graph-spectral spatial modes with periodic harmonic dynamics for structured motion not explained by the tool input. We evaluate the framework retrospectively on 12 surgical manipulation clips from three datasets. Observation referencing provides the largest gain, with a median within-clip error ratio of $0.598$ relative to the corresponding absolute simulation forecast. The optional periodic residual further improves forecasting when the remaining motion exhibits periodic structure. These results support observation-referenced deformation prediction as a practical building block for future surgical world models, digital twins, and generative simulators that must predict how tissue evolves under instrument actions.
items.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 1 table. Submitted to ICRA 2027

items.title_en: Beyond the Snowflakes: Disentangling Weather Effects from Confounding Meta-Factors in LiDAR Object Detection
items.title_zh: 超越雪花：在LiDAR目标检测中解耦天气效应与混杂元因素
items.abstract_en: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) is critical for autonomous perception, yet its performance is known to degrade in adverse weather. While existing literature models snow as atmospheric noise that degrades performance, our granular evaluation on the WADS-3D and CADC datasets reveals a counter-intuitive phenomenon: detection accuracy consistently improves as snow intensity increases. Through ablation study and meta-information analysis, we reconcile this by confirming that while falling snow acts as noise, its negative impact is outweighed by a dominant, concurrent factor: significantly increased object point count. We hypothesize that this object point count boost acts as a geometric enhancement, driven by snow accumulation increasing vehicle surface area and a shift from specular to diffuse reflectance. Our findings demonstrate that evaluating perception systems using broad weather-severity bins without accounting for correlated object-level data can lead to misleading conclusions about detector robustness. We conclude that accurate evaluation requires decoupling atmospheric noise from surface accumulation effects and outline future research to validate these physical models. The WADS-3D dataset is available at: https://digitalcommons.mtu.edu/wads-3d/.

items.title_en: HorizonNav: Geometry-Guided Video Diffusion for Anticipatory 3D Robot Navigation
items.title_zh: HorizonNav：面向预见性3D机器人导航的几何引导视频扩散
items.abstract_en: We present HorizonNav, a video diffusion-based framework for anticipatory robot navigation that transforms a single RGB image and a text prompt into a geometrically aligned representation of plausible surrounding 3D space. Given the initial observation and a textual description of the reconstruction objective, a vision-language model, guided by designed instructions, interprets the scene and constructs structured prompts for a video diffusion model. The resulting video sequence provides plausible future observations of the environment, which are subsequently processed using monocular ORB-SLAM3 for camera pose estimation and Video Depth Anything for dense depth prediction. Our central contribution is a geometry-guided depth alignment stage that combines the estimated camera poses with triangulated visual landmarks to constrain dense depth predictions across multiple views. This alignment improves the geometric consistency of the reconstructed 3D environment, addressing inconsistencies that temporal coherence of the generated video alone cannot resolve. The experimental evaluation of navigation in imagined 3D environment shows that across a 19-scene horizon study, planning-feasible scenes increase from 13/19 at P20 to 15/19 at P81, while successful RRT trials increase from 62/90 to 75/90. In a separate corridor study, 6 of 25 evaluable generated-camera trajectories violate the reconstructed collision constraints; RRT planner recovers feasible alternatives in 5 of those 6 cases. A larger archive contains 58 usable reconstructions from 67 attempted cases, of which 36 support a downstream plan and 22 do not, exposing reconstruction and free-space failure modes rather than hiding them without lidar. Across 15 corridor reconstructions, the mean reconstruction error is approximately 0.30 m at matched structural landmarks.
items.comment: 8 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE ICRA 2027

items.title_en: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
items.title_zh: LoopWAM：基于部署推演的闭环通用策略改进
items.abstract_en: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. We introduce \textbf{LoopWAM}, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies. Source-dependent noise sampling unifies behavior learning and action-conditioned world modeling, while quality steering and quality-weighted supervision retain full video supervision across qualities and regulate action imitation. Video and action tokens interact throughout parallel denoising, allowing learned consequences to inform action generation directly. On RoboChallenge Table30-V2, three deployment-and-training rounds raise success from 23.67\% to 43.33\%, a 19.7-percentage-point gain, with a final score of 56.80. LoopWAM also achieves 94.5\% average success on RoboTwin~2.0 and 49.5\% overall success on RoboCasa365 without additional embodied pretraining, obtaining the best overall results among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. On challenging shirt folding task, two rounds of deployment-driven improvement after single-task post-training raise success from 13.20\% to 55.56\%. These results demonstrate closed-loop improvement from mixed-quality experience under both multi-task learning and single-task post-training. \href{https://loop-wam.github.io/}{\textcolor{orange}{Project Page}}

items.title_en: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
items.title_zh: EgoExplorer：用于原位人类移动操作的视觉-运动-触觉观测平台
items.abstract_en: Learning humanoid loco-manipulation from human demonstrations rests on observing how locomotion, posture, and object interaction evolve together as tasks unfold. Scaling collection across diverse environments, in turn, favors lightweight, portable capture systems. Yet, existing datasets provide only partial views of this coordination. Thus, we introduce EgoExplorer, a 100-hour vision-motion-touch observatory of human loco-manipulation built with a wearable system. With an emphasis on professional activities, its continuous recordings align egocentric video with reconstructed whole-body motion, fine-grained finger articulation, and tactile observations, accompanied by step-level descriptions. To achieve this coverage with sparse body sensing, we develop the Calibrate-Complete-Constrain pipeline. Concretely, reusable calibration fixes participant geometry and sensor attachments before motion inference to disentangle mounting offsets from articulation. A temporal prior then completes unobserved joint motion, while layered constraints promote measurement agreement, temporal continuity, and geometric consistency, properties that motion plausibility alone does not guarantee. Against tracker-fitted references, the method reduces body-point error by 71.9% relative to the strongest baseline; matched evaluations also show gains in hand stability and contact estimation. Preliminary studies explore multimodal generation and conditioning alongside humanoid retargeting with whole-body control in simulation.

rm.usage: 采集人体全身运动与触觉的可穿戴数据集，面向人形移动操作，与RoboMaster轮式底盘和云台自瞄等任务关联很弱，基本用不上。

items.title_en: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
items.title_zh: 质量感知VLA预训练中的关键因素：基准与实证研究
items.abstract_en: How should demonstration quality be used during vision-language-action (VLA) pretraining to improve performance after target-task fine-tuning? We compare weighting, filtering, and conditioning across reward definitions and label granularities using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks. Within each VLA, we match demonstrations and training budgets. Additional comparisons examine pretraining data size and the roles of quality tags during fine-tuning and inference. Across three VLAs, we find that approach-aware episode conditioning improves mean success over plain behavioral cloning; conditioning and filtering favor episode and chunk labels, respectively, on average, with model-dependent reversals; and constant-tag fine-tuning improves mean success after conditioned pretraining with either tagged or untagged inference. We introduce AXIS-Bench to support these controlled comparisons. Built on crowdsourced simulation demonstrations, it provides recorded object and contact states for recomputing quality labels on shared trajectories. Replayable trajectories support workspace-aligned rendering and user-defined real-world target tasks. In our real-world experiment, simulation pretraining raises success from 9.6\% to 31.7\%. Project page: https://axis-bench.github.io/.

rm.usage: 研究示范质量对策略预训练的影响，若用战队采集的对战数据做模仿学习时可参考其质量加权/筛选思路，但属通用工具性结论，需较大改造。

items.title_en: EmbodiedEvo: Self-improving Coding Agents for Physical Intelligence
items.title_zh: EmbodiedEvo：面向物理智能的自我改进编码智能体
items.abstract_en: Bringing general-purpose agents into the physical world calls for an executable representation of physical intelligence. Compared with vision-language-action (VLA) models, which map observations and language instructions directly to actions, code makes control logic explicit and reusable. Code can serve not only as a policy representation but also as the workspace in which the agent solves a task. Rather than following a prescribed workflow of planning, execution, and verification, the agent can autonomously inspect the state, revise and execute code, and use feedback to choose the next step. The success of this SWE-style loop in digital environments motivates its extension to physical tasks. Yet physical execution remains prone to recurring failures. To retain and refine experience for later scenes, we introduce EmbodiedEvo, where a coding agent evolves reusable Skills and Lessons through feedback on a single Playground scene, then freezes the resulting harness for diverse new scenes. On RoboDojo-Sim, EmbodiedEvo achieves an average score of 44.48 and a success rate of 37.82\%, surpassing all officially verified results. Paired tests show the largest gains on memory-dependent tasks and successful reuse of coordinated procedures, while fine contact control remains difficult. Experience from stronger models also improves weaker executors: Astra's experience raises Sol and Luna's success rates by 8.86 and 5.50 percentage points over no experience. Compared with raw interaction history, Skills and Lessons achieve comparable task performance at 53.0\% lower execution cost.

rm.usage: 以代码作为策略表示并自省修改的智能体框架，可启发哨兵决策逻辑的自动生成/调试，但与赛事感知与控制环节差距较大，参考价值有限。

items.title_en: AutoAgent0: An Agentic Runtime for Safe Closed-Loop Driving
items.title_zh: AutoAgent0：面向安全闭环驾驶的智能体运行时
items.abstract_en: Safe autonomous driving requires more than accurate planning at a single frame: it demands reliable closed-loop execution in dynamic environments. Although end-to-end driving policies have advanced rapidly, the accumulated closed-loop errors, especially in unseen scenarios, can push vehicles into states from which the same policy struggles to recover. We address the challenge by treating closed-loop driving safety as a test-time execution problem. We introduce AutoAgent0, an agentic runtime and harness framework that augments existing driving experts with complementary detection skills, rule-based action verification, and feedback-driven recovery. To address inaccurate scene perception, an independent detection module constructs scene context using complementary perception skills, and a rule-based verifier checks proposed trajectories against this context before execution. When the nominal trajectories are unreliable, the orchestrator of the runtime activates Recovery Planning, where an agentic loop constructs alternative action proposals from action primitives and iteratively refines them using verification feedback. This design combines independent scene assessment with feasibility checks and online recovery, addressing both perception errors and the limited recovery capabilities of individual experts. Evaluations on Fail2Drive and NavSafe-$\infty$ demonstrate improved closed-loop robustness over single-expert execution in long-tail and safety-critical scenarios. These results demonstrate that runtime supervision can improve closed-loop robustness across multiple driving experts without retraining the underlying policies.

rm.usage: 面向闭环驾驶的智能体运行时，用规则+检测技能组合纠正在未见过场景下的闭环漂移，思路可迁移到哨兵自主导航中作为安全兜底与状态恢复模块。

items.title_en: Interaction Latents as Actions for Contact-Rich Manipulation
items.title_zh: 将交互潜变量作为动作用于富接触操作
items.abstract_en: Contact-rich manipulation requires robots to coordinate not only where to move, but also how contact and force should evolve throughout an interaction. Yet most robot policies represent actions primarily as motion trajectories, using tactile signals as inputs or auxiliary prediction targets without explicitly encoding contact dynamics in the action representation. We propose ILA (Interaction Latents as Actions), which uses decodable interaction latents that jointly capture the evolution of motion, contact, and force application as policy action units, providing a shared representation for action generation, evaluation, and offline improvement. We learn these latents through visually conditioned joint action-tactile reconstruction with a time-conditioned implicit decoder. Using them as flow-matching generation targets supports post-training of pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world action models (WAMs), as well as training flow-matching policies from scratch. A shared decoder maps generated latents to executable actions. For offline improvement, we learn a tactile-conditioned expert reference model from interaction latents encoded from expert demonstrations. The resulting expert-consistency rewards guide weighted learning from successful rollouts, while observation-compatible expert references guide correction of low-reward predictions from failed rollouts. Across three policy families, ILA improves success rates averaged over four real-world tasks by 21.0-36.5 percentage points relative to tactile-conditioned direct-action baselines. Ablations highlight the benefit of encoding contact evolution in action targets beyond tactile conditioning, while the same latent space supports expert-guided offline improvement. Project website: https://mrsecant.github.io/ILA/.

rm.usage: 用可解码的交互潜变量统一表达动作、接触与力，若工程机器人装配能量单元引入力/触觉反馈，可作为抓取-插入动作表示的参考思路，否则用处有限。

items.title_en: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
items.title_zh: 两个时钟：为何更大的推演批次在可验证奖励强化学习中学习更慢却按时失败
items.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) relies on costly model-generated responses, motivating larger rollout batches and square-root learning-rate scaling. Reported to approximately preserve progress per sample with one optimizer step per rollout, this rule is less understood in practical multi-step training. We develop a two-clock framework that separates the samples needed to make progress from those consumed before collapse. Under a local quadratic model, the square-root rule preserves first-order drift per sample but not progress: larger batches take fewer, longer updates and lose more to curvature, yielding a learning-rate-dependent critical batch beyond which sample efficiency degrades. A drift-threshold hypothesis predicts a complementary failure clock whose sample count remains approximately invariant along the square-root rule. Controlled GRPO experiments on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B across a $16\times$ batch range support both predictions. Ratio clipping delays failure, especially for larger batches, but the progress gap persists without it. Widening the clip trades stability for a transient speed gain. The progress gap reappears on another dataset, a general-purpose checkpoint, and a 7B model. Finally, we use the two-clock framework to derive a simple multi-step RLVR schedule: start below the critical batch and switch to a larger batch before failure. Our code is available at: https://github.com/WinstonLiyt/two-clocks-rlvr.

rm.usage: 分析大批量推演在可验证奖励强化学习中的学习速率与崩溃权衡，可为策略类强化学习训练调参提供经验参考，但过于理论、与具体环节距离远。

items.title_en: ForceWAM: Decoupling Future and Response Learning from Demo and Play Data for Contact-Rich Manipulation
items.title_zh: ForceWAM：从演示与玩耍数据中解耦未来与响应学习用于富接触操作
items.abstract_en: Expert demonstrations show how to complete contact-rich tasks, but provide limited coverage of how interaction forces respond to different actions. Task-agnostic play provides broader experience of contact dynamics without specifying task goals. To fully leverage these two types of data, we introduce ForceWAM, a force world action model that decouples knowledge of task-compatible interaction outcomes from knowledge of how local actions change contact. A world model learns from successful demonstrations to jointly predict future video and six-axis force/torque trajectories. Together, these futures describe the expected evolution of motion and contact during the task. A separate inverse dynamics model (IDM) learns from both task and play, mapping current observations and recorded visual-wrench futures to their associated robot actions. Play data thus provide knowledge of force responses for goal-directed execution. At deployment, the IDM reactively translates generated futures into actions, reusing them with fresh wrench feedback between world-model updates. Across real-robot force-regulated sliding, box flipping with and without disturbances, and ring placement, ForceWAM achieves $85$-$95\%$ mean success, surpassing world-modeling and reactive baselines. Our experiments further show that adding task-agnostic play data improves success by $15$-$45$ percentage points, demonstrating its value for learning contact-rich execution. Project page and code are available at https://force-wam.github.io/.

items.title_en: Collaborative Planning for UAV-UGV Teams under Operational Constraints via Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion
items.title_zh: 操作约束下UAV-UGV团队的协同规划：基于掩码误差有界神经符号扩散
items.abstract_en: Collaborative planning under operational constraints is essential for heterogeneous robot teams in large-scale missions. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) provide rapid area coverage but are limited by onboard energy, while Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) can serve as mobile recharging stations yet are constrained by road-network traversability. Effective collaboration must enforce operational constraints during execution while enabling parallel, coordinated actions. Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) have shown promise through token unmasking but have two key limitations: entropy-guided scheduling assumes distributional alignment and reliance on differentiable constraints for diffusion-time optimization. We propose Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion (MEND), which formulates collaborative planning as a conditional masked generative process to generate context-aware action sequences for UAV-UGV teams. MEND introduces a neuro-symbolic diffusion paradigm that constrains conditional masked diffusion policies at execution by reweighting the learned action distribution with a logic-induced admissibility indicator, thereby enforcing compliance with operational constraints. MEND introduces an error-bounded inference scheduling at execution that constructs the unmasking schedule by selecting positions with minimal predictive entropy over the constraint-aware action distribution, enhancing collaborative planning optimality under operational constraints. Extensive experimental results in simulation, on real-world maps, and with physical robot teams demonstrate that MEND advances UAV-UGV collaborative planning under operational constraints.

items.title_en: Contact Trajectory Prompting: In-Context Transfer of Contact-Rich Behaviors from a Single Demonstration
items.title_zh: 接触轨迹提示：从单次演示中上下文迁移富接触行为
items.abstract_en: In-context robot learning enables robots to acquire new behaviors from demonstrations without test-time parameter updates. However, visual and kinematic specifications alone may not distinguish contact-rich behaviors that share similar motions but require different interaction intensities or patterns. We propose Contact Trajectory Prompting (CTP), a framework for one-shot transfer of contact-rich manipulation behaviors. CTP encodes motion and contact information from a single demonstration into an ordered contact trajectory prompt that captures their temporal evolution and specifies the desired physical interaction behavior. During execution, the policy uses online sensory feedback to retrieve interaction-relevant information from the prompt, conditioning closed-loop action generation on the demonstrated contact behavior. Across real-world wiping, rotation, and insertion tasks on objects excluded from training, CTP achieves 78.7% overall success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 13.0 percentage points. Changing only the reference demonstration enables CTP to follow contact specifications for both intensity and direction, including an intermediate wiping force level and clockwise or counterclockwise cap rotation. These results demonstrate that contact trajectories serve as effective behavioral specifications, extending in-context robot learning beyond motion imitation to physical interaction transfer. Project website: https://ctp-robotics.github.io/project_page.
